title: Epistolae Duae
author: Nicetus Trevirensis Episcopus
source: Translated by Claude from tmp1160.tmp1160.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.

passages.original: Patres a quibus benedictionem exspectare debuisti, in exsilium transmisisti. Tum cum in ultima senectute tua componere et conjungere te ad Redemptorem tuum debuisti, ipse te, non alter, sed tu et te et tuos de- cepisti. Cum Lactantius, ut dicit, presbyter loca sancta per Gallias propter Domini misericordiam visitaret, ante nos apparuit; quæ legis, depreoavimus, et per Jesum Christum Redemptorem nostrum conjuravimus. Ergo litteris præsentibus Deum nostrum conjuravimus, insuper contestamur, ut et tu reve .tanis, et quantos perirc suasisti in horrenda persecutione, revertere provoces.
passages.english: The fathers from whom you ought to have expected a blessing you sent into exile. Then, when in your extreme old age you ought to have composed yourself and joined yourself to your Redeemer, you yourself, and no one else, you deceived both yourself and your own people. When Lactantius, a priest, as he says, was visiting the holy places throughout Gaul for the sake of the Lord's mercy, he appeared before us; what you are reading we have entreated, and we have adjured [you] by Jesus Christ our Redeemer. Therefore by the present letter we have adjured [you] by our God, and moreover we solemnly call on [you] to bear witness, that you too may return, and may call back to return all those whom you persuaded to perish in a dreadful persecution.
passages.notes: The text has several scanning errors: 'depreoavimus' is read as 'deprecavimus', 'perirc' as 'perire', and 'de- cepisti' as 'decepisti'. 'reve .tanis' is corrupt. It is taken as some form of 'revertaris' ('may return'). The clause 'quæ legis, depreoavimus' is obscure, and the rendering 'what you are reading we have entreated' is tentative. The addressee and the identity of this Lactantius are not established by the passage.
